answer:
For every integer \(m\ge7\),
\[
|K_m|\simeq \left(\bigvee^{s}S^{m-3}\right)\vee\left(\bigvee^{s+E}S^{m-2}\right)\vee\bigvee_{\substack{1\le q\le r\\\tau_q>1}}M(\mathbb Z/\tau_q\mathbb Z,m-3),
\]
with the following explicit finite arithmetic definitions.

Let
\[
\mathcal C_m=\{(A_1,A_2,A_3):A_i\subseteq[m],\ A_i\cap A_j=\varnothing\ (i\ne j),\ |A_i|\le2,\ \textstyle\sum_i|A_i|\le4\},
\]
\[
\mathcal R_m=\{(j;B_1,B_2,B_3):j\in[m],\ (B_1,B_2,B_3)\in\mathcal C_m,\ j\notin\bigcup_iB_i,\ \textstyle\sum_i|B_i|\le3\}.
\]
Order both sets lexicographically, encoding subsets by binary masks. For \(R=(j;B_1,B_2,B_3)\) and \(A=(A_1,A_2,A_3)\), put
\[
d(R,A)=\mathbf1_{A=B}+\sum_{i=1}^3\mathbf1_{\{A_i=B_i\cup\{j\},\ A_k=B_k\ (k\ne i)\}}.
\]
Set \((c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)=(1,3,9,24,54)\) and
\[
b_u=\binom mu\sum_{a=0}^{4-u}\binom{m-u}{a}c_a\quad(0\le u\le4),\qquad L=\min(b_0,b_1).
\]
Define \(\delta_0=1\), and for \(1\le q\le L\),
\[
\delta_q=\gcd_{\substack{R_1<\cdots<R_q\ \mathrm{in}\ \mathcal R_m\\A_1<\cdots<A_q\ \mathrm{in}\ \mathcal C_m}}\left|\sum_{\sigma\in S_q}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^q d(R_i,A_{\sigma(i)})\right|,
\]
where a gcd of an all-zero list is zero. Finally,
\[
r=\sum_{q=1}^L\mathbf1_{\delta_q>0},\qquad s=b_1-b_2+b_3-b_4-r,\qquad E=\frac{m^4+14m^3-m^2+34m+24}{24},\qquad \tau_q=\frac{\delta_q}{\delta_{q-1}}\ (1\le q\le r).
\]
The multiplicity of Moore spaces of a particular cyclic order \(t\ge2\) is explicitly
\[
\mu_t(m)=\sum_{q=1}^r\mathbf1_{\delta_q=t\delta_{q-1}}.
\]
